ch36.d.lambda: Wavelength $\lambda$ of the incoming light, shown as its colour
ch36.d.D: Distance $D$ from the slit to the screen
ch36.d.yp: Screen point for the source pair; drag the white dot on the screen
ch36.s.goal.cause: Cause of diffraction: every point in the slit acts as a new source (Huygens sources), and their waves interfere
ch36.s.goal.min: First minimum: each source in the upper half pairs with one half a slit below; every pair differs in path by $\lambda/2$ and cancels, so $a\sin\theta = \lambda$
ch36.s.obs.build: Play: the wave spreads out behind the slit and the screen builds up a wide central maximum and weak outer maxima
ch36.s.obs.pair: Default point (first minimum): the top source (blue) and the source half a slit below it (orange) differ in path by $\Delta L \approx 0.5\lambda$, and so does every other pair
ch36.s.obs.narrow: Slit width 1 μm: the central maximum spreads wide ($\sin\theta_1 = \lambda/a$)
ch36.s.obs.wide: Slit width 6 μm ($a \gg \lambda$): the light goes nearly straight through, a bright band about as wide as the slit (the shadow of geometric optics)
ch36.s.obs.lambda: Wavelength 400 → 700 nm: the same slit spreads the light wider
ch36.s.assume.model: 2D model: the slit is a row of Huygens point sources, amplitude $\propto r^{-1/2}$, no reflection from the barrier
ch36.s.assume.scale: The screen distance is scaled down to μm to fit the stage. For wide slits the Fraunhofer condition ($D \gg a^2/\lambda$) fails and the minima move slightly away from $a\sin\theta = \lambda$
ch36.s.assume.sources: The 10 dots in the slit are for illustration; the wave is computed with sources spaced at most $\lambda/2$ apart
ch36.d.theta: Angle $\theta$ from the slit to the screen point; dragging the dot on the graph also changes it
ch36.d.N: Number $N$ of sources across the slit, one phasor arrow each
ch36.ph.goal.chain: Each source's wave is one phasor arrow; the phase difference of neighbouring sources is the angle between neighbouring arrows
ch36.ph.goal.min: The sum $E_\theta$ runs from the start to the end of the chain. When the chain closes into a circle the sum is 0: a minimum
ch36.ph.obs.zero: Angle 0°: all arrows in a line, the sum is the largest, $E_m$
ch36.ph.obs.min: Default (14.5°, near the first minimum): the two edges of the slit differ in phase by $\phi = 360°$ and the chain closes once around a circle
ch36.ph.obs.second: Larger angles: the chain winds more than once, leaving a small sum (an outer maximum), then closes again after two turns (second minimum, $a\sin\theta = 2\lambda$)
ch36.ph.obs.a: Narrower slit: smaller phase difference at the same angle, the chain curls less, so the central maximum is wider
ch36.ph.obs.N: Changing the number of sources (settings) leaves the minima in place: they are set by the edge-to-edge phase difference $\phi$
ch36.ph.assume.far: Screen very far away (Fraunhofer diffraction): rays from all sources are parallel
ch36.ph.assume.draw: The slit on the left is an enlarged sketch; the graph is the sum of $N$ sources ($N \ge 8$: the same minima as $(\sin\alpha/\alpha)^2$ of a continuous slit, outer maxima slightly higher for small $N$)
